samples.execution: When imported as sitecustomize, creates a hidden /tmp sentinel and forks. The parent returns; the child calls setsid and repeatedly calls _tick with silent exception handling and a 3600-second delay. _tick fetches a routing text file, selects its first stripped line as a host, fetches http://<host>/payload, compiles that body and executes it in a fresh __main__ namespace. No stdio redirection, encoded stage, credential collection or self-deletion appears.
samples.judgment: Unattended remote source execution through an interpreter startup surface and an externally selected host tips the verdict. Actual installation as sitecustomize is not established by the renamed filename: the content guard establishes the intended surface. The example-like GitHub endpoint is not corroborated infrastructure. The remote payload and runtime success are unknown.

samples.identity: Standalone Microsoft Entra OAuth password sprayer
samples.execution: Explicit __main__ entry loads configured user and password lists. Password-major nested loops submit username/password grant forms to the Microsoft common OAuth token endpoint using a Teams first-party client ID and a legacy Teams/Electron user-agent. TLS verification is explicitly disabled. Per-account waits use configured jitter; each complete password round has a random 30-90 second wait. On a nonempty access token, prints the successful credentials and retains (user,password,refresh_token) tuples in memory. The main caller discards the returned list. Does not redeem tokens against other services, transmit them to an attacker endpoint, install persistence or fetch executable stages. A success without refresh_token raises KeyError; network/JSON errors are uncaught.
samples.judgment: Bulk live guesses across independent accounts plus reusable-token retention are an offensive credential-acquisition purpose. An authorized assessment remains plausible, but no authorization, tenant ownership, invocation or deployment context is supplied. The docstring describes emulation of TeamFiltration, not proof that this is that product. No third-party conviction or scanner score determines this judgment.

samples.execution: Sequentially clears eight event logs, including Sysmon, PowerShell and Defender Operational channels; invokes reagentc /disable; runs an external DiskPart script from TEMP; overwrites unused space on D: using cipher /w; flushes the DNS resolver cache with output suppressed; writes a file-lock/contact-for-restoration claim. Does not encrypt live files or disable Defender scanning. DiskPart script contents are absent, so recovery-partition removal is unproven. There is no command-success gate or privilege-elevation code; privileged operations can fail and later commands still run.
samples.judgment: Recovery disablement, destruction of deleted-data recovery material, broad forensic-log clearing and an extortion-style note jointly tip the verdict. An isolated DNS flush or DiskPart script is ordinary maintenance. Comments say Settra-style but do not identify an actual malware family. Privileges, the external script, invocation context and operational success are unknown.

Retained the hostile WinRE/script/trace-destruction combination, renamed and relocated by its supported recovery effect. No unseen DiskPart commands are inferred.
